text:
In the era of BD, economic development has also entered a new stage. The combination of BD technology and industrial development effectively promotes the development of industrial economy [1]. At this stage, China has very limited fossil energy, which restricts largely the development of industrial economy. In addition, the use of a large amount of fossil energy has caused serious damage to the ecological environment in China. To change this situation, China has been developing RE, which also has a practical significance, such as improving the ecological environment and coping with climate change [2]; the development of RE can certainly improve China’s energy security level and reduce its excessive reliance on imported energy, create new areas of economic growth and promoting sustained economic growth.

In recent years, the content of RE has attracted extensive attention from the academic community, many scholars had conducted related research on it. Li [3] argued that it was necessary to develop RE to better deal with the energy crisis and ecological deterioration. Based on the analysis and summary of the international energy development, it was proposed that China should formulate a RE development path in line with its own national conditions and explore actively energy development strategies suitable for different stages of development. Ager and Lapkin [4] argued that it would be a potential way to us RE to convert carbon dioxide into fuel and chemicals to alleviate the increase of carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere and ocean acidification, and also found that carbon dioxide could be electrochemically reduced to hydrocarbons by using RE. To strengthen the penetration of RE in urban power demand, DeRolph et al. [5] proposed a spatial framework to match the energy supply and demand of the entire grid, thus realizing the distribution of urban RE plans.

Gernaat et al. [6] argued that climate-dependent RE might be affected by future climate change, so he proposed to use climate and comprehensive assessment models to assess the different impacts of climate on RE. Egli et al. [7] argued that the research and development of RE technology usually required high costs in the early stage, so it needed to have good financing conditions. For this reason, he made some research on the macroeconomic conditions and empirical impact of the RE finance industry. Gu et al. [8] summarized the latest progress of machine learning methods in the development of RE materials, and demonstrated the application of machine learning methods in RE technologies, including catalysis, batteries, solar cells and crystal discovery. However, these scholars’ research on RE was not comprehensive enough, and further research on RE based on BD could play a good role [9].

The theoretical mechanism connecting Big Data (BD), Renewable Energy (RE), and economic growth is structured below. Big data significantly promotes economic growth by optimizing the production, management, and integration of renewable energy, which is reflected in the following three aspects.

(1)

Optimize the production and management of renewable energy.

Big data analysis on weather, historical data, and real-time environmental conditions can predict the power generation of solar and wind energy, helping energy suppliers adjust their operational strategies and balance supply and demand contradictions.

(2)

Reduce energy costs and enhance economic returns.

The upstream and downstream integration of the renewable energy industry chain (such as cooperation between photovoltaic modules and power generation enterprises) optimizes resource allocation through big data collaboration and reduces production costs.

(3)

Promote the coordinated development of energy and other industries.

Big data supports distributed optimization, reducing energy waste and lowering consumer costs through real-time monitoring and demand response systems.

The research on BD is very popular in all walks of life, and there are also relevant research reports on energy. Anthony et al. developed a layered architecture using Application Programming Interface (API) in BD for regional energy management to provide energy information intelligence, and to support energy sustainability decision-making and promote mining operations [10]. In fact, the hierarchical architecture collected energy data and provided data to consumers who produced, consumed, shared and sold RE, so as to better improve the energy consumption of smart grid [11]. Zhang et al. proposed an energy-aware network physical system for energy BD analysis and hidden production anomaly detection. Considering the complexity and dynamics of manufacturing process, he proposed an analysis method of hidden production anomalies driven by energy BD based on deep belief network [12].

According to the literature research above, in the era of big data, the relationship between renewable energy and economic growth can be summarized as the follows.

(1)

Positive promotion effect

Big data technology significantly improves the efficiency of renewable energy utilization by accurately predicting energy demand, optimizing supply chains, and scheduling, thereby reducing energy costs and promoting economic growth. For example, smart grids can reduce energy waste and enhance supply stability through real-time data analysis.

(2)

Parameter adjustment effect

Studies show that the energy regeneration rate and technological progress are key parameters affecting the stability of economic growth. Increasing the energy regeneration rate or technological level can extend the peak consumption period, making the economic growth trajectory smoother. Governments can further amplify the positive impact of renewable energy on the economy by adjusting discount rates through fiscal and tax policies and strengthening technological investments.

(3)

Structural transformation drive

The increased proportion of renewable energy will promote the upgrading of industrial and consumption structures, creating new economic growth points in areas such as new energy vehicles and smart transportation.

Previous related researches had mainly the following three deficiencies: (1) Theoretical framework is incomplete. Existing research mostly focuses on a single dimension (such as the direct impact of renewable energy on economic growth), lacking a systematic theoretical model that integrates big data technology, energy transformation, and economic models. (2) Insufficient research on regional differences. Although studies have shown that the impact of renewable energy on economic growth varies in different regions (such as the east and the west), the analysis of regional heterogeneity combined with big data technology is still relatively weak. (3) Long term effects and lack of policy synergy. Most studies are based on short-term data (such as 1–5 years), making it difficult to reveal the long-term cumulative effects of big data-driven deployment of renewable energy on economic growth. Meanwhile, the synergistic mechanism between policy tools such as subsidies and tax incentives and big data technology has not been fully explored.

In sum, there are few studies linking BD, RE with economic growth in the current literatures. In the era of big data, the relationship between renewable energy and economic growth presents a complex but positively interactive pattern. The synergistic effect between renewable energy and economic growth is constantly deepening through technological innovation and policy optimization. Therefore, it can be assumed that there is a definite positive correlation between the growth of renewable energy production and sustainable economic growth, which is exactly the problem that this article aims to study.

To fill the research gap mentioned above, this paper uses a new RE consumption assessment method integrating time series production simulation to conduct the research on the more efficient production, storage and consumption of RE, analyzes the impact of RE on economic growth and puts forward that the economic growth model of the new era is the circular economy model [13], aiming at contributing to the promotion of the sustainable development of the economy through this economic model in the era of big data.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: "Evaluation of the new model of RE economic growth in the context of BD" section; section 3, RE Consumption Assessment Method Integrating Time-series Production Simulation; "Experimental results and analysis" section; "Discussion" section, Conclusions section.

Impact of BD era on economic growth mechanism

In the era of small data, the main ways to promote economic growth include the increase of domestic demand, investment and export [14]. In the era of BD, these methods have already shown many shortcomings. In the small data environment, it is difficult to analyze the deficiencies at the structural level in an all-round way. In the era of BD, rich and complete data is available for comprehensive analysis and calculation. The application of big data in the economic growth model of renewable energy encompasses the entire process from forecasting to trading, comprehensively enhancing industry efficiency and competitiveness. Specifically, its applications include four aspects: precise forecasting and scheduling, intelligent operation and maintenance with cost optimization, marketization and trading innovation, as well as policy and planning support. Its effects manifest in three key areas including efficiency improvement, cost reduction, and market stimulation.

From the analysis results, under the BD environment, the economic growth effect has obvious differences, which are mainly reflected in the following two aspects:

Impact on micro factors, product supply and demand

In the era of BD, the available data is more comprehensive, and the data analysis technology is also better. With the promotion of the third industrial revolution, the manufacturing industry has gradually moved towards intelligent, digital and scientific production, and the traditional demand and supply structure of product elements have also changed [15]. The birth of 3D (3 Dimensions) printing technology has led to the complete overthrow of the “long tail effect”. As a product of BD, the emergence of this technology has also well met the personalized needs of consumers. The market can also provide the heterogeneous goods they need according to the different needs of consumers in a timely manner. While manufacturers maximize profits, consumers’ purchase needs would also be met. While stimulating consumption, it also drives economic growth.

Impact on the driving force of macroeconomic growth

In the BD environment, data plays a very important role in daily production activities. Therefore, the data analysis industry has also begun to rise, and the continuous progress of digital technology has made the data analysis method more advanced. The traditional consumption, project investment and export are all based on the data for specific analysis. Data acts as a medium, which promotes the integration and development of traditional industries and modern intelligent society [16]. With the support of BD technology, intelligence and information technology can be combined with industrial development to continue to promote the development of productivity to enhance the level of industrialization and the economic growth. The development of digital, intelligent and information industries has gradually become a new driving force for economic growth.

Renewable energy

Development status of RE in China

RE refers to a kind of energy that can be continuously regenerated and utilized in nature, which can be inexhaustible [17]. There are many kinds of RE, and their classification is shown in Fig. 1, mainly including solar energy, water energy, wind energy, biomass energy, tidal energy and other energy.

Strong growth momentum of installed capacity

In recent years, with the strong support of the national industrial policy, the scale of investment in RE in China has been expanding, and the installed capacity of energy has also been rising. The installed capacity of RE in China from 2020 to 2024 is shown in Table 1.

In terms of investment, China’s total investment in the RE industry has been relatively high in recent years, which once became the largest investor in the world. In terms of energy installation, the scale is also expanding, and the installed capacity of solar and wind power also continues to occupy the first place in the world. The proportion of China’s installed RE capacity in 2024 is shown in Table 2.

According to the "China Renewable Energy Development Report 2024" published by the China Hydropower Planning and Design Institute, China's renewable energy development had been rapid, with installed renewable energy capacity accounting for 56.4% of the country's total power generation capacity in 2024. In terms of installed capacity and power generation, as of 2024, China's cumulative installed capacity of renewable energy reached 1.889 billion kilowatts, of which wind and solar power generation totaled 1.83 trillion kilowatt hours, accounting for about 18.5% of the total power generation. Renewable energy generation increased by 17.3% year-on-year, demonstrating strong growth momentum. In terms of technological progress, China has made significant breakthroughs in renewable energy technology, including advances in hydropower, wind power, and photovoltaic technology. The conversion efficiency of photovoltaic cells has significantly improved, and the single unit capacity of wind turbines has reached a new historical high. The development prospects of renewable energy in China are broad. It is expected that in the following several years, with the continuous progress of technology and sustained policy support, the installed capacity and power generation of renewable energy will continue to grow, further promoting China's energy transformation and achieving sustainable development goals [18].

Continuous improvement of supporting policies

To promote the use of RE, China’s National Energy Bureau has also launched a series of favorable policies to support its development. The formulation of these policies has greatly promoted the sound development of various RE and related industries. China has also gradually moved from a “major producer” of RE equipment to a “major producer”, and the RE industry has also made new progress in equipment development, technological innovation, industrial management system optimization and other aspects.

Significance of the development of RE

Help to protect the environment and cope with climate change

At this stage, China’s ecological and environmental problems are very serious, and the ecosystem is relatively sensitive. Large-scale exploitation and use of non-RE have caused serious harm to the environment. In the energy consumption structure, the proportion of coal is relatively high, which leads to the continuous increase of carbon dioxide emissions and has a great impact on climate change. RE has the advantages of high efficiency and cleanness, low carbon and environmental protection, and sustainable use [19]. Therefore, the vigorous promotion of RE plays a vital role in improving the energy structure, protecting the environment, saving energy and reducing emissions, and improving climate change.

Help improve China’s energy security level

China is a country with abundant coal resources and inadequate oil and natural gas. Due to the large demand for oil and natural gas in China, its import dependence of oil and natural gas is high. At the current stage, China’s oil dependence on foreign countries is more than 60%, and natural gas dependence on foreign countries is also more than 40% [13]. To reduce its international energy dependence, China has been considering adjusting its existing energy structure. Today, the development and utilization of RE has gradually become the main direction of energy utilization in the future, which is also an important measure to ensure national energy security.

Help open new areas of economic growth

China has a rich variety of RE, which is distributed in many regions, so the development prospect of RE is good [20]. Moreover, different regions have certain conditions for development and utilization, and can flexibly use local resources to promote the development of RE industry. With the continuous development and innovation of RE itself in the future, RE will promote the development of different industries such as energy measurement, equipment manufacturing and electric vehicles, and industries related to RE will also become the focus of China’s deepening industrial reform and establishing a new economic system of the current generation.

Current problems of RE

Although the development potential of RE is large, there are still some shortcomings, which can’t replace completely the position of non-RE in a short time. If these problems cannot be effectively dealt with, it is likely to have a certain negative impact on economic growth during the energy transition period. At present, the problems of RE are shown in Fig. 2.

Power generation costs remain high

There are many factors affecting the development of RE, among which cost and price are the most important [21]. In recent years, the cost of wind power generation and solar power generation has decreased significantly. However, compared with the cost of thermal power generation, it is still very high. Under the current market economy system, its competitiveness is poor. At this stage, smart grid and energy storage technologies related to power generation costs are not mature enough for large-scale application. Therefore, the application cost is high. In order to reduce the power generation cost of RE, it is necessary to continuously improve the relevant technical level.

The subsidy gap is under great pressure

Due to the limited additional costs and benefits of RE, the subsidies are also delayed for a long time, and the fast-speed development of RE is easy to lead to a growing gap in subsidies for RE. The subsidy cannot be received in time. When faced with a shortage of funds, many enterprises were unable to carry out effective financing, thus resulting in the dilemma of capital rupture. Now, China has gradually entered the stage of power parity, and the power price is also becoming reasonable, so the power generation subsidies will soon be canceled.

Inadequate innovation in technology and development mode

At this stage, there are still many deficiencies in RE technology. Especially in terms of innovation, there is a lack of comprehensive basic scientific research, and the scientific research force is insufficient. The comprehensive research and development system integrating production, education and research is not perfect. The worst aspect is that its key technology depends mainly on other countries. The development and utilization of RE is not diversified enough, and its potential in distributed utilization is also very limited, which lacks sufficient innovation.

RE and circular economy model

Impact of RE on economic growth

For a long time, coal, oil and other fossil fuels have been the key driving force to promote economic development. However, fossil energy has a strong scarcity and would cause serious damage to the environment, which seriously restricts the sustainable development of the economy. In the long run, the development of RE will play a good role in promoting sustainable economic growth [22]. Therefore, the vigorous development of RE is more conducive to promoting technological innovation, industrial structure adjustment and optimization to achieve stable economic development.

Diversified energy structure is conducive to economic growth

The production and uses of RE and ordinary energy are roughly the same, so it can be a good substitute for other energy sources. From the perspective of cost, the marginal cost of RE generation is lower, while the response of thermal power to the price fluctuation of natural materials is more intense. In terms of price elasticity, compared with thermal power generation, RE power generation is a better alternative. In addition, there is a very close relationship between fossil energy and China’s energy security, especially under the uncertainty of oil supply. Therefore, the increase of RE consumption can make the energy structure more diversified, thus effectively ensuring the orderly development of the economy.

RE has an industry-leading effect

The core of competition for renewable energy is technological advantage, rather than the resource monopoly of traditional fossil fuels. Technological leadership reduces production costs through innovation diffusion, improves energy conversion efficiency, and ultimately achieves competitive energy prices. The sustainable development of renewable energy relies on cost reduction. Technological progress and large-scale production are the key paths to reducing costs, and marginal costs may approach zero, according to the Theoretical Analysis of Renewable Energy Cities by Lou [23]. The development of RE industry can promote the development of macro-economy and provide a good development environment for related industrial projects. At the employment level, the employment scale of the traditional energy industry will be sharply reduced by the impact of the RE industry. At the same time, the rise of new industries will also drive the rise and development of related industries, so that there will be new employment demand and more employment opportunities in the market.

RE promotes the improvement of technology

The RE quota system can significantly improve its competitiveness in the field of power engineering, and can also effectively encourage power generation enterprises to accelerate the rational allocation of resources and technological research and development [24]. In addition, RE power projects account for a high share in the electricity power market and continues to promote thermal power enterprises to ensure production capacity, which can also accelerate the innovation of industrial technology to improve power generation efficiency and reduce costs. This will promote the overall development rate of the energy industry and accelerate the industrial transformation and upgrading. In addition, since the RE industry chain covers different industries, there are close joint effects between industries.

Circular economy mode

The essence of circular economy is a green ecological economy, including the comprehensive utilization of waste, clean production and recycling. Compared with the traditional economy, the key point of circular economy is to reuse the available materials for many times. The circular economy model is shown in Fig. 3.

Under the circular economy model, there is little or no waste in the process of production and consumption. Namely, there is no real waste in this mode, but the location of the whole resource is incorrect [25]. The birth of this model has effectively improved the contradiction between economic development and the environment. This requires that people should always adhere to three principles when carrying out economic activities, namely, the principles of resource, reuse and recycling. Among them, resource utilization refers to the reduction of material quality and pollutant emissions in the production and consumption links, so as to achieve resource conservation; reuse means to ensure adequate use of services and products, to ensure adequate use of services and products, to improve the utilization rate of packaging materials and products, and to resolutely resist the excessive use of disposable goods; recycling is to strive to achieve that the used goods can form renewable resources for reuse.

The circular economy model, through efficient resource utilization and waste regeneration, is highly compatible with the sustainable characteristics of renewable energy and has become a core element driving green economic growth. The following are specific reasons: (1) Efficient utilization of resources and synergy with renewable energy. The circular economy is based on the principles of "reduction, reuse, and resource utilization", reducing the exploitation of natural resources and lowering energy consumption. (2) Technological innovation and industrial upgrading. Circular economy promotes technological breakthroughs in resource recycling, giving rise to new forms of green industry (3) Social participation and behavioral changes. The circular economy advocates for the public to reduce disposable consumption, participate in garbage classification, and resonate with the popularization of renewable energy sources such as electric vehicles and energy-efficient buildings. (4) Systematic environmental benefits. The circular economy reduces waste emissions and resource waste, lowers carbon intensity, and aligns with the emission reduction goals of renewable energy.

At this stage, the economic development model has changed from “conquering nature and transforming nature” to a circular economy model advocating “harmony between man and nature”. To build a harmonious society and achieve sustainable economic development, circular economy needs to be developed. Its prerequisite is to follow the ecological law and carry out economic activities within the sustainable range of the ecological environment.

Sequential production simulation method

The time series production simulation method mainly simulates the specific operation state of the system software. The time scale can be divided into two types. In short cases, it usually varies from a few hours to dozens of hours; in a long time, it usually varies from several months to several years. The output characteristics and load characteristics of RE are simulated and analyzed. Based on the priority consumption of RE, a power balance model is built, and then the operation of the power grid is simulated step by step. The time-series on RE consumption data spans the period from 2020 to 2024, and such data is used for the statistics of different RE values in these figures and table.

The maximum output value of RE accepted by the system is expressed as follows:

$$\mathbf q=\max\left(W_\mathbf r^\text{e}-\sum_\text{i=1}^\text{n}W_\text{i,yu}^\text{e}-\sum_\text{j=1}^\text{n}W_\text{j,q}^\text{e}\right)$$

(1)

In Eq. (1), q represents the output value of RE, Wre represents the load value of the outgoing power of RE, \(\sum\limits_\text{i=1}^\text{n}W_\text{i,yu}^\text{e}\) represents the total loss of the load value caused by the transmission line of the outgoing power of RE, \(\sum\limits_\text{j=1}^\text{n}W_\text{j,q}^\text{e}\) represents the total loss of the load value caused by the transformer equipment of the outgoing power of RE. The unit of power is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (1). The parameter sources are from China National Bureau of Energy for all 8 equations from (1) above to Eq. (8).

Constrained condition

Power balance constraints

Power balance constraints can be expressed as follows:

$$W_q+W_{yu}+W_o+W_{yj}-W_e=W_r$$

(2)

In the Eq. (2), \(W_q\) represents the thermal power output value; \(W_{yu}\) represents the hydropower output value; \(W_o\) represents the photovoltaic output value; \(W_{yj}\) represents the wind power output value; \(W_e\) represents outgoing power; \(W_r\) represents the load value. The unit of power output is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (2).

System reserve capacity constraints

The system reserve capacity constraint can be expressed as follows:

$$\text{A}\geq\text{W}_{\max}\times\left(\text{s}+\text{d}\right)+\text{W}_\text{pre}\times\alpha+\text{W}_\text{f}$$

(3)

Among them, A represents the spare capacity that the system may need; \(\text W_{\max}\) represents the expected maximum load; d represents the proportion of emergency reserve; \({W}_\text{pre}\) represents the expected output power of RE; \(W_f\) represents the maintenance reserve capacity. The unit of capacity is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (3).

Thermal power unit output constraints

$$W_{down}\leq W\leq W_{up}$$

(4)

Among them, \(W_{down}\) represents the minimum technical output of thermal power unit; \(W_{up}\) represents the rated output. The unit of power is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (4).

Ramp rate constraint of thermal power unit

In a short period of time, the output value of RE would change greatly, and it is easy to abandon wind and light. Ramp constraints of thermal power units can be expressed as follows:

$$\frac{P_{t+1}-P_t}{P_t}\leq\frac{R_u}{2}$$

(5)

$$\frac{P_{t}-P_{t+1}}{P_t}\leq\frac{R_D}{2}$$

(6)

Among them, RU represents the ramp-up rate and RD represents the ramp-down rate. Pt is the power at the time of t, Pt+1 is the power at the time of t + 1 in Eq. (5) and (6).

Ramp-up rate is the rate of change in output or load over time, typically used to describe the gradual increase in power generation, user concurrency, or other variables over a specified period. It is often expressed as a change per unit time (e.g., MW/min). Ramp-down rate refers to the rate of gradual reduction in volume, amount, or rate. For example, when a project is scaled down, the ramp-down rate determines how quickly the operations or resources are adjusted to match the new scale.

Output constraints of hydropower units

The output constraints of hydropower units are expressed as follows:

$$0\leq W_\text{yu}\leq W_\text{up}$$

(7)

In the formula, \(W_\text{yu}\) represents the output value of hydropower unit, and \(W_\text{up}\) represents the rated output value. The unit of output is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (7).

External power constraint

When the output of RE in one place is relatively abundant, it can be considered to transmit the surplus power to other places, and its power transmission would be constrained by the power of the external power transmission line, which is expressed as Fig. 4 and formula (8).

$$W_{tran}\leq W_{line}$$

(8)

In the formula, \(W_\text{tran}\) represents the excess RE power to be transmitted, and \(W_\text{line}\) represents the maximum power of the transmission power line. The unit of power is kilowatts (kW) in Eq. (8).

In fact, the surplus RE power to be transmitted can be saved into RE power storage system when the transmitted RE power exceeds maximum power transmission capacity of the power transmission line and reserved for the future use either locally or out of town. Many cities with surplus RE power output transmit their saved surplus power to other cities needing these power output at night.

To verify the effectiveness of the time series production simulation method, this paper collected the historical big data of the power grid in Turpan (a typical city in Xinjiang, China) where RE consumption experienced significant increase from 2020 to 2024.

The status of Turpan's power system in terms of storage, demand response, and transmission network limitations is as follows. In terms of current situation of power storage system, the power grid in Turpan has built 38 new energy transmission lines with a total length of 612.1 km, which transport clean energy from new energy stations to various places. In December 2024, the first batch of units of the Huaneng Turpan wind power project were successfully connected to the grid and equipped with a 200,000 KWH energy storage system. This is the first new energy project in the local area to have supporting energy storage facilities. In terms of the demand response mechanism, faced with the surge in demand for new energy grid connection, Turpan Power Supply Company has innovatively implemented the "one-stop service + three-stage control" model, covering the entire process of early planning, engineering construction, and acceptance grid connection services, significantly improving the grid connection efficiency of new energy projects. For example, the acceptance and grid connection of Tangshan Haitai New Energy Technology project was completed in December 2024, with an expected annual revenue of 524 million Yuan. In terms of transmission network restrictions, the Turpan power grid faces the following challenges: (1) New energy consumption pressure. In 2024, new energy generation accounted for nearly 92% of the total electricity sold in the grid, but the local consumption capacity is insufficient, resulting in a large amount of electricity needing to be sent out. (2) Stability pressure on the power grid. New energy accounts for up to 64%, leading to a decrease in system regulation capacity and greater balancing pressure during the winter supply guarantee period. (3) Construction of transmission channels. By constructing new 220 kV transmission projects and 35 kV to 220 kV lines, the power grid structure will be continuously strengthened, but it still needs to be improved.

Turpan City has achieved coordinated development of energy storage through various projects. For example, the Tangshan Haitai project has improved RE power generation stability through molten salt thermal storage technology. At the same time, the demand response mechanism guides users to adjust their electricity consumption behavior through economic incentives, ensuring the flexibility of the power system and promoting the consumption of renewable energy. The RE power output transmission project is accelerating and is expected to further optimize the regional power grid structure after completion by the end of 2025 to meet the demand for new energy transmission.

Turpan relies on the construction of distributed photovoltaic modules and energy storage systems to form a full industry chain layout of "solar thermal + photovoltaic + energy storage". The distributed power grid extends the industrial chain through inverter assembly, photovoltaic module processing, etc., improving the utilization rate of local renewable energy [26]. But there are also some limitations in renewable energy output. The seasonality and uncertainty of renewable energy generation stem mainly from fluctuations in natural conditions (such as significant seasonal variations in solar, wind, and hydro power), manifested as intermittency, volatility, and seasonality, posing challenges to grid scheduling and power supply stability. This paper conducted a simulation test of RE consumption data in Turpan from 2020 to 2024. The datasets come from the relevant statistical data on renewable energy generation in these annual statistical reports.

To increase the contrast of the experiment, the traditional method was also used to carry out the contrast experiment. The experimental results are as follows.

RE absorption value test

In this experiment, two algorithms were used to test and analyze the RE consumption value, and the test results are shown in Fig. 5.

Figure 5A shows the test of RE consumption value under the algorithm in this paper (RE), in which, RE consumption value equals to the sum of final energy consumption value (FECV) and energy processing and conversion loss (EPCL), namely, RE = FECV + EPCL, the energy loss under traditional algorithm (REt) is not included because the significant increase of the storage capacity of the RE electricity power, which has been enough to save unconsumed RE electricity power in Turpan from the year 2020 to the year of 2024 when the related big data is used to construct the model above and the model below.

Figure 5B shows the test of RE consumption value under the traditional algorithm (REt), in which, RE consumption value equals to the sum of final energy consumption value (FECV), energy processing and conversion loss (EPCL) and energy loss (EL), namely, REt = FECV + EPCL + EL.

The data in Fig. 5 that the test results of the two algorithms on the absorption value of RE were different, the absorption value of RE refers to the actual amount of renewable energy generation absorbed by the power grid, reflecting the power grid's capacity to absorb and utilize electricity generated from renewable energy. In Fig. 5A, when the time reached 1000 h, the absorption value of RE was 837 MW, which reached the lowest value. When the time reached 4000 h, the absorption value of RE was 1582 MW, which reached the highest value. The difference between the highest value and the lowest value was 745 MW. In Fig. 5B, when the time reached 1000 h, the absorption value of RE reached the lowest, which was 537 MW. When the time reached 2000 h, the absorption value of RE reached the highest, which was 1336 MW. The difference between the two was 799 MW. To sum up, under the method in this paper, the absorption value of RE was generally higher. This showed that this method could effectively improve the power transmission performance of RE, so that it could transmit more electricity at the same time.

The statistical analysis of the data in Fig. 5A indicates that the mean is 1174.2 MW, the variance is 99,792.7 at 99% confidence interval. The proposed algorithm in Fig. 5A was also repeated in scenarios in 2 other cities in Xinjiang (Hami and Wujiaqu) with continuously increasing consumption of RE power and the related statistical data [27, 28] and findings from these 2 cities also support completely our conclusion we made from the scenario in Turpan as shown above. In other words, the robustness of the research results is strong.

Abandoned RE value

To further compare the differences between the two algorithms, this paper also carried out relevant test and analysis on the value of abandoned RE (in MW) of Turpan, which refers to the electricity generated by renewable sources such as wind and solar power that is wasted and cannot be effectively utilized due to grid regulation requirements, transmission network limitations, or market price factors from 2020 to 2024, and the test results were shown in Fig. 6.

Figure 6A shows the value test of abandoned RE under the algorithm in this paper. Figure 6B shows the test of abandoned RE value under the traditional algorithm (REt). Figure 6 shows that the test results of the two algorithms on the value of abandoned RE had obvious differences. In Fig. 6A, the value of abandoned RE shows different changes at different times. When the time reached 1000 h, the value of abandoned RE was 432 MW; when the time reached 4000 h, the energy value reached the minimum, which was 314 MW; when the time reached 5000 h, the energy value reached the maximum, which was 475 MW. The difference between the minimum energy value and the maximum energy value was 161 MW, which showed that the fluctuation range of the overall energy value was relatively smaller. In Fig. 6B, the value of abandoned RE was also different in different time. When the time was 1000 h, the value of abandoned RE reached the maximum, which was 639 MW; when the time was 4000 h, the value of abandoned RE reached the minimum, which was 396 MW; the difference between the two energy values was 243 MW, which shows that the overall fluctuation range was relatively larger. From the above data, the value of abandoned RE was generally lower under this method. It shows that the more RE consumption could be exchanged, which could effectively reduce the consumption rate of RE.

In a comparison between the value of abandoned RE in Fig. 6A and the value of abandoned RE in Fig. 6B, the value of abandoned RE in Fig. 6A is much less than the value of abandoned RE in Fig. 6B at 5 different level of time in terms of hours from 1000 to 5000, which indicates that the proposed algorithm in Fig. 6A can reduce a lot of abandoned RE than the traditional algorithm (REt) in Fig. 6B as shown in Table 3, in which a statistical analysis including the mean (x̄), variance (S2) of the value of abandoned RE and the related significance test at 99% confidence interval (or significance level at α = 0.01) is made. In statistical analysis in the following Table 3, when the p-value (assuming probability) obtained from hypothesis testing is less than 0.01 (P < 0.01), it indicates that the research findings are statistically significant at a 99% confidence level. The calculation formulas for the mean (x̄) and variance (S2) are given: x̄ = (x₁ + x₂ + … + xₙ)/n, S2 = [Σ (xᵢ—x̄)2/(n—1)], where n is number of samples.

From the 2 values of variances (S2) above in Table 3, it can be concluded that there is a significant difference (= 8099.3–4270.3 = 3829) between the 2 variances.

The related error analysis, sensitivity analysis, and benchmark validation are made below.

Error analysis

In error analysis for data in Fig. 6A, the mean standard deviation method quantifies errors by calculating the data mean (x ̄) and standard deviation (s). Here are the specific steps:

(1)

Calculate the mean

The mean (x ̄) is a representative of the trend in the dataset, calculated using x̄ = (x₁ + x₂ + … + xₙ)/n, the calculation result x̄ = (432 + 348 + 419 + 314 + 475)/5 = 1988/5 = 397.6.

Among them, x ᵢ is a single data point, and n is the total numbers of data.

(2)

Calculate standard deviation

The standard deviation (s) reflects the degree of data dispersion, and the calculation formula is: s = √[Σ(xᵢ—x̄)2/(n—1)] = (1190.25 + 2460.16 + 457.96 + 6988.96 + 5990.76)/(5—1) = 65.36.

The denominator of the sample standard deviation is n-1, and the denominator of the population standard deviation is n.

(3)

Error quantification

The mean represents the concentrated position of the data, and the standard deviation represents the range of error. The smaller the standard deviation, the more concentrated the data, and the smaller the error; On the contrary, the error is relatively large.

Sensitivity analysis

This article uses a one-by-one exclusion method to perform repeated analysis by removing one individual data point in turn from 5 samples. Then, the results are compared. If the conclusion is consistent after the change, it indicates robustness; If there is inconsistency, the robustness is not strong.

To compare the differences between the two algorithms more comprehensively, this paper also analyzed the proportion of abandoned RE based on the related statistical data in Table 4, which is shown in Fig. 7.

Figure 7A shows the proportion test of abandoned RE under the algorithm in this paper. Figure 7B shows the proportion test of abandoned RE under the traditional algorithm (REt). The proportion of abandoned RE was inversely proportional to the consumption of RE. The lower the proportion of abandoned RE, the higher the consumption of RE and the greater the electricity that can be transmitted. Figure 7 shows that under different algorithms, the test results of the proportion of abandoned RE also had certain differences. In Fig. 7A, the proportion of abandoned RE was relatively low, and it remained within 10% in general. When the time reached 4000 h, the proportion of abandoned RE reached the highest, which was 8.32%. When the time reached 5000 h, the proportion of waste RE reached the lowest, which was 5.25%. The difference between the two was 3.07%, and the difference was small. It is obvious that the overall energy share did not change significantly. In Fig. 7B, the proportion of abandoned RE would be higher, and the overall proportion was more than 10%. When the time reached 1000 h, the proportion of abandoned RE reached the highest, which was 14.32%. When the time reached 2000 h, the proportion of waste RE reached the lowest, which was 10.24%. The proportion difference between the two was 4.08%, which was relatively large. To sum up, under this method, the proportion of abandoned RE was lower. It shows that this method could effectively reduce the generation of abandoned RE, thus increasing the consumption of RE and reducing costs.

Under the backdrop of the era of big data, the research of this paper makes a theoretical contribution on the relationship between renewable energy and economic growth, which mainly focuses on their mutual promotion, with greater emphasis on quantitative analysis and the exploration of dynamic mechanisms. The research focuses mainly on the difference between the RE consumption value and the abandoned RE value under the traditional algorithm (REt) and that under the new algorithm, the RE consumption capacity was improved due to the reduced abandoned RE (or waste RE) in consequence. This is a research contribution which was not covered by previous studies.

Relevant measures to promote RE

Development of RE projects

The organic combination of centralized and distributed development of RE projects is adhered to in China. New projects in the rational layout of industries such as rocky desertification control, facility agriculture, fishery and aquaculture, and rural revitalization and development are prioritized. The centralized photovoltaic industries such as photovoltaic power generation in rocky desertification, agro-photovoltaic complementation, and fish-photovoltaic complementation are being developed according to the time. The large-scale construction of wind power generation is being conducted, and the wind resources in various regions are also fully utilized. The large-scale construction of onshore and offshore wind power generation resources is conducted to promote the development and construction of onshore decentralized wind power generation. The construction of biomass cogeneration power stations is also promoted, thus making full use of local various waste resources and converting them into agricultural biomass energy.

Improve relevant policies for RE development

The trading system of the RE electricity market is improved to ensure that the electricity trading channels among all provinces are sufficiently smooth, and the direct trading between the supply and demand market entities is being strongly supported [29]. The electricity spot market trading system is established. The standardization construction of the electricity market is also guided and promoted, and the absorption capacity of RE is being improved according to the marketization method. The favorable policies for the research and development and application of energy storage technology are deeply implemented, and the energy storage price system corresponding to the market-oriented operation of electricity is established and improved. The security system and relevant policies for the coordinated development of RE and multi-party development are accelerated and improved, especially the incentive policies related to resettlement, land resource utilization and ecological environment protection, such as hydropower projects and biomass energy.

Main measures for developing circular economy model

Formulating relevant policies and forming an effective incentive mechanism

To develop the circular economy, the authority of the government needs to be fully played, and the guidance, encouragement and assistance of preferential policies can be fully played as far as possible. The government can formulate and optimize relevant industrial policies, and actively study and introduce relevant subsidy policies, preferential tax policies, reward and punishment mechanisms that match the development of circular economy to promote the orderly development of circular economy. At the same time, it is also necessary to establish and improve the relevant system and system of government procurement and determine the legal proportion of renewable products. The government promotes green procurement as an example to encourage the public to actively participate in the purchase of renewable products.

Improving the environmental awareness of the masses

With the help of public opinion, news reports, network media and other means, the circular economy and intensive social model can be deeply publicized and promoted to improve the public’s awareness of environmental protection. Specifically, the purpose and significance of promoting circular economy are publicized. In the publicity and education theme activities, environmental protection knowledge manuals can be distributed to the public to enhance the public’s awareness of environmental protection. At the same time, in primary and secondary schools, circular economy can be publicized to achieve the effect of education on students. Students would lead parents to establish environmental awareness, and parents would act on social groups to form a broader influence. In addition, the development of circular economy can also guide the public’s consumption behavior and concept to a certain extent, so that they can establish the concept of green consumption. When purchasing products, they can choose more products with environmental protection signs.

The economic growth model in the era of big data is undergoing profound changes, with its core feature being the transformation of the driving mechanism for economic growth, where data becomes a key factor of production and achieves structural improvement in total factor productivity.

The digital economy takes data as the core input, and realizes dynamic optimal allocation of resources through Internet, Internet of Things and other technologies. For example, intelligent manufacturing systems rely on real-time interaction between the Internet of Things and big data to reduce production line failure rates by about 30% and increase inventory turnover efficiency by more than 25%. The supply chain collaboration platform based on big data can control the error rate of resource allocation within 2%, which is more than 15 percentage points more optimized than traditional models [30]. This networked collaborative mechanism promotes the transformation of economic growth from scale and speed based to quality and efficiency based.

In terms of the mutual promotion mechanism, the economic growth drives renewable energy development, as economic levels rise, social environmental protection requirements increase, prompting enterprises to invest more in clean energy, at the same time, capital accumulation supports technological research and development as well as infrastructure construction, such as the initial funding needs for solar power plants and wind farms; in terms of the economic growth promotion by renewable energy, the renewable energy industry creates employment opportunities and promotes the development of other industries (such as new energy vehicles and smart grids) through technological spillover effects, the transition to green energy reduces carbon emissions, indirectly promoting sustainable macroeconomic growth and economic structure optimization, which can be supported by the related data on the continuous increase of both RE electricity power consumption and GDP in China in recent years as indicated in the following Table 5.

From the data in the Table 5, it is clear that both the renewable energy electricity power consumption and its percentage in all electricity power consumption had been increasing at an annually rate of over 30% from 2021 to 2025 (except in 2021), meanwhile, the GDP had been increasing at an annual rate of over 5% (except in 2022), this is convincing evidence showing the long-term mutually reinforcing relationship between renewable energy electricity power.

consumption and economic growth.

In addition, there are also other key influencing factors including technological progress and policy support. The maturity of technology directly affects cost and efficiency. For example, advancements in solar panels and energy storage technology reduce investment costs, but technological bottlenecks still need to be overcome (such as the stability of wind energy storage). The policy support such as government subsidies, tax incentives, and other policies can reduce enterprise investment risks, but it is necessary to balance short-term costs with long-term benefits. The limitations of this research include the insufficient data covered by the research scope which may lead to inaccurate reflection of the new model of renewable energy economic growth under the background of big data and the selection of sample areas that are not typically representative due to the seasonality and uncertainty of renewable energy generation in selected regions with sample data used in this article, and the insufficiently long period of just 5 years for the sample data.

title: Data centers could brown the landscape, or green the power sector
authors: Mia Hollie, Christopher Wink, Holly Quinn, Sarah Huffman, Alice Crow, Sam Markowitz, Kaela Roeder, Andrew Goldner, Maria Eberhart, Maxine Van Nortwick
description:
As the new industrial revolution of AI data centers sweeps the region, it’s just as difficult to crystal ball its effects on the landscape and environment.
More than 4,300 data centers, or facilities that store servers and offer computing services, dot the country.
Virginia, home to over 600 data centers with another 500+ in planning, is considered the “data center capital of the world.” Other top data center hubs sit in Texas, Arizona, Georgia, California and Illinois, said Dan Diorio, the vice president of state policy for the Data Center Coalition, a membership group for data center operators.
Data centers proposed near Pittsburgh, including the Homer City campus, are primarily expected to use natural gas to fuel their operations.
The state has already revived old power generation sites to support new data centers.
text:
When the Edgar Thomson Works opened in 1875, few could have imagined that Southwestern Pennsylvania would one day be dotted with former steel mill sites, now called brownfields, in states of repair and reuse.

As the new industrial revolution of AI data centers sweeps the region, it’s just as difficult to crystal ball its effects on the landscape and environment.

Over the next 150 years, some environmental advocates and researchers say Southwestern Pennsylvania could see a deluge of hyperscale data centers — those that cover 10,000 square feet and typically use at least 100 megawatts of electricity. They worry that the facilities will siphon large quantities of local energy and are concerned about effects on water supplies.

As these resources are pushed to their limits, though, a full transition to clean energy could be in store for the future.

The data center buildout could also turn out to be narrower than anticipated, as operators focus on “right-sizing” their operations in anticipation of a bursting artificial intelligence bubble.

Poised for growth, but with caution

High-quality coal and river access drove the development of mills and steel towns, and history may be repeating itself.

Yvonne Sorovacu, an environmental scientist at ProtectPT, said she imagines a future in which little separation exists between data centers and the power generation sites that power them, particularly in rural areas. Established in 2014, Protect PT advocates against fossil fuel activities in Westmoreland and Allegheny counties. In Westmoreland County’s Upper Burrell Township, she said fracking well pads could surround the proposed data center campus there in the future.

“When you think about that buildout, I think about Texas and I think about the landscape there and what it looks like from space, and I’m like, ‘Prepare for parts of our counties to look like that,’” she said.

More than 4,300 data centers, or facilities that store servers and offer computing services, dot the country. Virginia, home to over 600 data centers with another 500+ in planning, is considered the “data center capital of the world.” Other top data center hubs sit in Texas, Arizona, Georgia, California and Illinois, said Dan Diorio, the vice president of state policy for the Data Center Coalition, a membership group for data center operators.

The energy demand for data centers in the U.S. will triple by 2030, according to some estimates. As the industry quickly grows in the near term to fill demand, Diorio said the commonwealth has stood out as a tertiary market — far behind Virginia or Texas, but also “one of the strongest growing markets out there.”

Pennsylvania doesn’t publicly track data centers, but some estimates show roughly 130 data centers are operating, proposed or under development. At least 12 sites are planned for Southwestern Pennsylvania, according to the crowdsourced Data Center Proposal Tracker.

The commonwealth’s well-established energy industry could make it the next hotbed of hyperscale data centers, said Lauren Posey, an environmental policy advocate for ProtectPT. Only Texas bests the commonwealth in natural and shale gas production, and Pennsylvania outranks all other states in its number of operating coal-fired power plants.

The next few decades, however, will be marked by data center operators “right-sizing” their infrastructure, Diorio said. Broad concerns of an AI bubble loom over his members’ heads, and future buildouts will be informed by demand.

“You don’t want to underbuild because then you’re not meeting demand, but you don’t want to overbuild because then you have a stranded asset where you’re not providing a service and you have infrastructure still on the ground that you spend billions of dollars in capital on,” he said.

Karen Feridun, a co-founder of the renewable energy advocacy group Better Path Coalition, said some global markets are already scaling back their hyperscale data center production.

“There have already been examples in China, among other places, where they’re scaling it down so much, that this kind of massive, hyper-scaler that’s gonna take up football fields worth of space … that’s just not gonna be necessary,” she said.

“I think that we’re gonna end up with a lot of stranded assets.”

Energy limits may compel clean power

Rob Altenburg, PennFuture’s senior director for energy and climate, said building more power generation only to meet the demands of increasingly large data centers won’t be sustainable over the long run — in the same way that additional lanes on a highway won’t cure traffic issues.

“You can’t build your way out of a congestion problem. You have to plan your way out of it, and the [electrical] grid works a lot the same way,” he said. PennFuture is an environmental advocacy organization.

He noted that data centers still face a comparatively energy-efficient competitor.

“The human brain uses about 20 watts, so you can do intelligent things with a lot less power,” Altenburg said. “This is the big engineering problem: How do we make these big things use much less power to accomplish their goals? I think that’s probably gonna be a trend, but we’re not heading [in] that direction yet.”

Central processing units, as well as graphic processing units, serve as the brains of data centers. Several of the small pieces of hardware are stored in servers to carry out general computing, graphics processing and AI-related tasks.

Researchers are increasingly finding ways to make these chips more efficient, and a new market of local startups are finding early success from building more efficient AI chips or energy-saving coding techniques.

While the commonwealth’s Governor’s Responsible Infrastructure Development (GRID) Standards don’t require data centers to use less energy, they do require operators to commit to building or purchasing their own electric energy before taking advantage of tax credits and permit fast-tracking programs.

The state will need to produce cheaper forms of energy, such as wind or solar, Altenburg said.

Julie McNamara, the director of federal energy policy for the Union of Concerned Scientists, also predicts the country’s future energy generation will be “unequivocally clean.” The group researches and advocates for policies related to climate change. McNamara said the future could also present new renewable energy options that extend beyond what exists today.

Companies known for utilizing hyperscale data centers — Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon included — have already been contracting increasing amounts of clean energy. The four companies now collectively contract around 135 gigawatts of clean energy, five times more than they did just four years ago.

Water use may drop

Pennsylvania’s waterways still carry raw materials to mills as they’ve done since the industrial revolution. In this revolution they serve a different, critical function by supplying water to cool data centers.

Most small-scale data centers, such as the ones that dot Pittsburgh’s North Shore and Downtown, use air to cool their servers, while hyperscale data centers often use water instead in order to save energy.

The Susquehanna River Basin Commission in March modified its agreement with Amazon Data Services regarding its daily “consumptive use” — meaning the water never returns to its source — of 129,000 gallons in Luzerne County’s Salem Township. For comparison, the average restaurant consumes around 300,000 gallons of water in a single year. Another data center proposed for nearby Hazle Township would use 67,000 gallons of water daily if approved by the commission.

Most power generation plants also need water to cool off, creating a data center-driven “double hit” on the water supply, Altenburg said.

Diorio, however, said that data center operators “don’t get a pass on any water discharge or water use, water intake… We have to follow the same rules that any other development follows.”

He pointed to a study conducted by Arizona State University in which researchers found data centers there consume less water than beverage and semiconductor producers.

More efficient water uses are already emerging. The data center slated for Springdale Borough, for instance, plans to use a closed-loop system that requires only an initial withdrawal of water equivalent to an Olympic swimming pool. Newer techniques also directly cool down processors rather than submerging entire servers in water.

Still, the state’s water suppliers, electric grids and ratepayers will hit their limits at some point, Altenburg said, pushing data centers to become ever more efficient.

Near-term concerns of pollution, health risks

McNamara said she’s most concerned about what happens in the interim.

“I think that 150-year ballpark is incredible to imagine, that future place. But I worry so much about the near-term years to come. There is so much at stake in these next few years.”

In addition to potentially straining local energy and water supplies, data centers can cause air pollution by running on-site, gas-fired turbines. The resulting noise pollution can also affect nearby people and wildlife.

And when “you have dirty, noisy businesses, you usually have an environmental justice issue,” Altenburg said, “because they tend not to put them in the wealthy neighborhoods.”

There are also indirect effects, such as air pollution from off-site power generation sites and harm to organisms that live in the waterways from which water is extracted for industrial use.

But similar to how operators must follow water use regulations, Diorio said that they must also follow the Environmental Protection Agency’s regulations for backup generators and other on-site power infrastructure.

In its latest report, the U.S. Global Change Research Program noted communities living near oil and gas extraction sites would face increased health issues in the future. Previously mandated by Congress, the research program produced annual reports on climate change. An industry-wide effort to reduce emissions could still leave those communities burdened with pollution, according to the report.

Data centers proposed near Pittsburgh, including the Homer City campus, are primarily expected to use natural gas to fuel their operations.

The state has already revived old power generation sites to support new data centers. Even if a complete transition to renewable energy occurred tomorrow, remediating land where oil infrastructure used to exist poses a major financial hurdle to states such as Pennsylvania, McNamara said.

“The past is shouting at us: ‘Don’t do this again. We’ve made this mistake before.’”

Mia Hollie is the economic development and housing reporter for Pittsburgh’s Public Source. She can be reached at mia@publicsource.org.

This story was fact-checked by Emma Folts.

text:
Rivian has expanded its optional extended-warranty program ‘Rivian Care’ to 31 US states — up from six a month ago — marking the largest single expansion since the protection plan debuted as a Texas-only pilot in May 2025.

The update adds 25 states to the program’s footprint and, for the first time, lists the R2 mid-size SUV alongside the R1T, R1S and Rivian Pre-owned vehicles as eligible models.

Deliveries of the R2 to external customers began on June 9.

The warranty program’s expansion arrives as thousands of new owners prepare to take delivery over the coming months.

Rivian Care launched in May 2025 as a pilot restricted to a small group of Texas owners.

X user and Rivian owner Chris Hilbert, who first mentioned the expansion on Wednesday, also mentioned the program’s debut at the time.

The pilot shifted its geographic footprint multiple times over the following year. An earlier expansion late in 2025 offered coverage in Georgia, Maine, Minnesota, New York, South Carolina and Texas.

A subsequent update in early June dropped Maine, Minnesota and South Carolina while adding Colorado, Illinois and Oregon, settling the list at six states.

The latest update quintuples that count.

Rivian Care is now available in Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Maine, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, New York, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Oregon, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Texas, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.

Maine, Minnesota and South Carolina — which were dropped from the six-state list — have also returned.

Several of Rivian‘s largest ownership markets remain absent, however.

California, the single biggest EV market in the country, is not on the list. Florida, Pennsylvania, Washington, Ohio, New Jersey, Massachusetts and Virginia are also excluded.

Rivian has said on its support page that it plans to roll out the program across the country in the future and invites owners in uncovered states to register interest through their accounts.

What the Program Covers

Rivian Care is an optional vehicle protection program administered by United Service Protection Corporation, which operates under the trade name Assurant.

Owners can choose one or both of two separate products.

The Vehicle Service Contract covers the cost to repair or replace the high-voltage battery, drivetrain, mechanical components, safety systems and more after a covered breakdown, once the Rivian New Vehicle Limited Warranty ends.

Coverage extends to motors, electronics, advanced driver-assistance and safety systems, infotainment, sensors, cameras and mechanical systems including heating, ventilation and suspension.

Select wear-and-tear items are covered from the start of the plan.

The Vehicle Service Contract acts as secondary coverage to the factory warranty, and the two may overlap, Rivian has noted.

The Preferred Vehicle Protection plan addresses everyday damage that the factory warranty does not cover, including windshield damage, tire and wheel damage and paintless dent repair.

Both plans are transferable to a new owner, possibly for a fee — a feature Rivian and Assurant have positioned as a way to support resale value.

Replacement parts used under either plan may be new, used, remanufactured or non-original-equipment, according to the contract terms.

Rivian does not publish fixed pricing for the program.

Owners receive a quote after applying, and the company states that coverage costs less when purchased while the factory warranty is still active.

Buyers preparing to take delivery of a new vehicle can add Rivian Care during the purchasing flow.

Owners who have already taken delivery can log into their Rivian account and complete an interest form.

Gap Post-Factory Coverage

Every newly produced Rivian comes with a New Vehicle Limited Warranty that runs for four years or 50,000 miles for comprehensive bumper-to-bumper coverage.

Battery and drive-system coverage extends further, to eight years and up to 150,000 miles depending on the battery pack.

Standard battery packs carry coverage to 120,000 miles, while the larger and Max packs reach 150,000 miles.

Vehicles also carry eight-year corrosion protection.

The Vehicle Service Contract is designed to take over after that comprehensive coverage expires, addressing the high-cost battery and electronics repairs that concern owners keeping their vehicles long term.

Owners outside the covered states have previously turned to nationwide third-party providers such as Xcelerate and EV-Assure, which offer extended coverage for Rivian models regardless of location.

R2 Ramp

The warranty expansion coincides with the early weeks of R2 deliveries.

On Tuesday, reservation holders began receiving their estimated times to order.

Rivian is targeting 20,000 to 25,000 R2 deliveries this year within a full-year guidance range of 62,000 to 67,000 vehicles.

Adding the R2 to the eligible model list ensures the program is available to the cohort of buyers entering Rivian‘s ecosystem at a lower price point, with the R2 Performance starting at $57,990 and a $45,000 Standard trim expected in 2027.

Rivian ended the first quarter of 2026 with 100 service centers, 39 showrooms and nearly 700 mobile service vehicles.

The company has said it aims to operate more than 150 service centers by the end of 2027 and plans to expand its mobile service fleet by 50% this year.

Founder and Chief Executive RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as the most important launch in the company’s history.

text:
— Says bank ready to finance battery production, faults foreign rating agencies, hails Dangote Refinery

Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The President and Chairman of the Board of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), Dr. George Elombi, has urged African countries to stop exporting raw lithium and instead develop a thriving electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturing industry on the continent.

Speaking at the bank’s Mid-Year Media Roundtable in Abuja, Elombi said Africa must leverage its vast mineral resources to drive industrialisation and economic development rather than exporting raw materials.

He said Afreximbank was ready to finance the establishment of EV battery manufacturing plants across the continent.

“African mineral resources must work for Africa’s development. EVs are the future of transportation, and the use of lithium to produce EV batteries is taking centre stage in the EV industry.

“Africa must take its position in the EV industry. We have lithium. We should produce EV batteries at home. We simply have to produce them here. There is enough money in Africa to manufacture batteries in Africa.

“If you know anyone who is interested in EV battery production, bring them to me. But if you see someone looking for funding to export lithium, don’t bring them to me,” he said.

Elombi also called on African governments and institutions to work together to repatriate African capital held abroad and channel it into the continent’s development.

He stressed that African resources and investments should primarily serve Africa’s economic transformation.

Faults Western Rating Agencies

The Afreximbank president accused some international credit rating agencies of maintaining a biased perception of Africa and consistently underrating African financial institutions despite their improving financial strength.

He said some rating agencies initially dismissed Afreximbank as too small and questioned its trade finance mandate, arguing that trade could not drive development.

“They were questioning the very treaty that established the institution and gave it its mandate. We could not accept that. They also seemed to suggest that trade could not drive development, whereas trade has always been the bedrock of economic growth,” he said.

According to Elombi, Afreximbank has since proved its critics wrong by expanding its operations and becoming one of Africa’s leading development finance institutions.

He noted that one of the rating agencies had revised its assessment after acknowledging the bank’s growing role in financing trade, infrastructure and economic transformation across Africa.

“From being considered irrelevant in 2014, they now acknowledge that Afreximbank has become highly relevant and even too important to fail because of its strategic role in Africa,” he said.

Elombi argued that some Western rating agencies continue to assess African institutions using outdated assumptions, particularly regarding liquidity and risk.

He explained that Afreximbank had deliberately diversified its funding sources away from traditional Western markets by securing financing from Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

According to him, Western funding, which previously accounted for about 80 per cent of the bank’s borrowing, now represents only about 12 per cent, while Asia and Africa each contribute about 38 per cent, with the Middle East accounting for around 12 per cent.

He said some rating agencies had interpreted the reduced reliance on European capital markets as a weakness.

“When we depended largely on Western liquidity, they said our funding profile was diversified. Now that we have genuinely diversified our funding sources, they claim our liquidity has weakened simply because we are not borrowing as much from the Eurobond market. That does not make sense,” he said.

Elombi maintained that funding from Asia and Africa had proved reliable, more affordable and better aligned with Africa’s changing trade patterns.

He disclosed that Afreximbank also introduced a central bank deposit programme to mobilise idle African capital held overseas, attracting deposits from African central banks and corporate institutions.

According to him, the bank deliberately built excess liquidity ahead of anticipated global economic shocks to ensure it could continue supporting African commercial banks when international financing became constrained.

He said that despite acknowledging the bank’s strong liquidity position, some rating agencies still downgraded its liquidity profile because it had not recently issued Eurobonds.

“We raised funds where they were cheaper and more accessible to support African trade. The fact that we chose not to borrow from the Eurobond market at a particular time should not be interpreted as financial weakness,” he said.

Elombi urged that African financial institutions should be assessed based on their fundamentals and developmental impact rather than traditional Western benchmarks.

Hails Dangote Refinery

The Afreximbank president also praised the Dangote Refinery, describing it as a model for Africa’s industrial development.

He reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to supporting the refinery following the $2.5 billion financing deal signed in March and pledged additional support as the company expands into other African countries.

According to him, Africa needs more large-scale industrial projects similar to the Dangote Refinery to achieve sustainable economic growth and self-reliance.

text:
The nation’s largest electricity grid — which includes Maryland, Washington D.C, and a dozen other states — received a green light from the Trump administration on Tuesday to require data centers and other large customers to turn on back-up generators during this week’s heatwave.

The order, signed by U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, allows PJM Interconnection to tap into diesel back-up generators, battery arrays and more as a “last resort” to prevent power shut-offs as temperatures climb to dangerous heights in the latter half of the week.

“Currently, there are tens of gigawatts of readily available backup generation that have remained largely untapped,” Wright wrote in his order. “Deployment of backup generation resources … can prevent avoidable blackouts, thereby saving lives and reducing costs to the American people.”

Wright’s emergency order will last through July 3. It does not apply to certain facilities serving a critical need, including hospitals, 911 call centers, water treatment plants, air traffic control towers and defense facilities.

But it does include AI data centers, which have wreaked havoc on PJM’s markets because of their immense energy demands.

PJM also received approval from the U.S. Department of Energy on Tuesday to require power generating facilities to operate to fuel the grid — even if they would surpass pollution limits by doing so.

“Because the additional generation may result in conflict with environmental standards and requirements, I am authorizing only the necessary additional generation on the conditions contained in this Order,” Wright wrote.

It is up to PJM to call upon the power plants to operate and set the parameters, and it must notify the Department of Energy when additional power generation resources are tapped to go beyond its pollution allowances.

Power generators are to comply with environmental regulations, including recordkeeping requirements, to the “maximum extent practicable” during the emergency. According to PJM officials, the order could result in exceedances of sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, carbon monoxide, ammonia and wastewater releases. The order expires at 11:59 p.m. on July 3.

PJM is predicting high demand through the weekend, peaking on Thursday, when demand is projected to set a new record for the grid at 166,304 megawatts, surpassing the previous record of 165,563 megawatts, set in 2006.

Throughout Central Maryland, the National Weather Service is predicting high temperatures just below 100 on Wednesday, followed by high temperatures between 102 and 104 degrees Fahrenheit from Thursday through Saturday.

PJM is operating under a hot weather alert through July 3. For July 1, the grid operator has also issued a “maximum generation alert,” which calls on transmission and generation owners to defer any possible equipment maintenance or testing activities until the heatwave passes.

The grid operator has also issued a “load management alert,” advance warning that it could use demand response programs on July 1, programs that pay customers who sign up to allow for energy reduction during emergencies.

In anticipation of the heat wave, Maryland utilities have been offering customers tips to conserve power whenever possible in order to lower their bills.

The lists include setting thermostats at higher temperatures such as 78 degrees, using appliances later in the day, cooking outdoors when possible and using fans for cooling, but turning them off when no one is present in a room.
